name: terminal/port-and-process
title: Port and process
summary: Find which process uses a port or the most memory, and hand the user the command that would stop it.
when: Use when a port is already in use or a process is eating memory and the user wants to know what and why.
steps: Call run_command with ss -ltnp to list listening ports, or lsof -i :PORT for the port the user names.
Call run_command with ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -15 to find the processes using the most memory.
Call run_command with ps -o pid,ppid,user,cmd -p PID and readlink /proc/PID/cwd to see what started it.
Call run_command with systemctl status name or docker ps when the process looks like a service or a container.
Check the pid, user and start time against what the user expects, and say which process is the one they mean.
If nothing listens on the port, say so plainly and call run_command with journalctl -u name -n 50 before guessing.
Give the user the exact command that stops the process in a code block and say what it does; do not run it.
next: The final answer must name the pid, user and command line holding the port or the memory, and give the exact stop command without running it.
